'''Patrick L. Holland''' (born 1971) is the Conkey P. Whitehead Professor of Chemistry at [[Yale University]]. Holland's research focuses on low-coordinate and [[High Spin Complex|high-spin]] [[Coordination complex|coordination complexes]] of iron and cobalt, that react with small molecules such as [[Alkene|alkenes]], [[Aromatic compound|arenes]], and [[Nitrogen|N<sub>2</sub>]].

== Early life and education ==
Holland was born in 1971 in Pennsylvania.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Chemistry Seminar: Dr. Patrick Holland, Yale University|url=https://calendar.hope.edu/event/chemistry_seminar_1372|access-date=2021-06-01|website=Hope College Calendar|language=en}}</ref> During his childhood, he lived in Ohio until he was 12, when his family moved to Florida.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Guest Speaker: Dr. Patrick Holland from Yale University {{!}} IMNI|url=https://www.brown.edu/research/institute-molecular-nanoscale-innovation/news/2014-05/guest-speaker-dr-patrick-holland-yale-university|access-date=2021-06-01|website=www.brown.edu}}</ref> Holland attended [[Terry Parker High School]] in [[Jacksonville, Florida]], graduating in 1989. He then attended [[Princeton University]], graduating with his A.B. in 1993. Following graduation, Holland pursued graduate studies at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] with Prof. [[Robert G. Bergman]] and Prof. [[Richard A. Andersen (chemist)|Richard A. Andersen]], earning his Ph.D. in 1997. At Berkeley, Holland synthesized [[Cyclopentadienyl complex|cyclopentadienyl]] nickel [[Coordination complex|complexes]] with [[Metal amides|amido]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Holland|first1=Patrick L.|last2=Andersen|first2=Richard A.|last3=Bergman|first3=Robert G.|date=1996|title=Synthesis, Characterization, Isomerization, and Reactivity of Dimeric Cyclopentadienylnickel Amido Complexes|url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/full/10.1021/ja952882l|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=118|issue=5|pages=1092–1104|doi=10.1021/ja952882l|bibcode=1996JAChS.118.1092H |issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription}}</ref> and [[Alkoxide|alkoxo]] ligands.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Holland|first1=Patrick L.|last2=Andersen|first2=Richard A.|last3=Bergman|first3=Robert G.|last4=Huang|first4=Jinkun|last5=Nolan|first5=Steven P.|date=1997-12-01|title=Monomeric Cyclopentadienylnickel Methoxo and Amido Complexes: Synthesis, Characterization, Reactivity, and Use for Exploring the Relationship between H−X and M−X Bond Energies|url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/full/10.1021/ja971829p|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=119|issue=52|pages=12800–12814|doi=10.1021/ja971829p|bibcode=1997JAChS.11912800H |issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Holland|first1=Patrick L.|last2=Smith|first2=Michael E.|last3=Andersen|first3=Richard A.|last4=Bergman|first4=Robert G.|date=1997-12-01|title=X-ray Crystal Structures of Cp*Ni(PEt3)X [X = Br, O(p-C6H4Me), NH(p-C6H4Me), S(p-C6H4Me), OCH3, CH2C6H5, Me, H, PEt3+]. == Independent career ==
Holland began his independent career in 2000 at the [[University of Rochester]] as an assistant professor.<ref>{{Cite web|last=CJ.LiMcGill.ca|first=Contact Information Contact: CJ Li Email|title=CCVC: Patrick Holland - Nitrogen Binding and Fixation using Iron Complexes|url=https://www.mcgill.ca/chemistry/channels/event/ccvc-patrick-holland-nitrogen-binding-and-fixation-using-iron-complexes-293032|access-date=2021-06-01|website=Department of Chemistry|language=en}}</ref> He was promoted to associate professor in 2005, and full professor in 2010.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Pat L. Holland CV (12-20)|url=https://holland.chem.yale.edu/sites/default/files/files/Holland%20CV%2012-20.pdf}}</ref> In 2013, Holland moved to Yale University, where he is currently a professor of chemistry. In 2021, he was awarded the title Conkey P. Whitehead Professor of Chemistry.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-07-14|title=Patrick Holland appointed Whitehead Professor of Chemistry|url=https://news.yale.edu/2021/07/14/patrick-holland-appointed-whitehead-professor-chemistry|access-date=2021-11-21|website=YaleNews|language=en}}</ref>

== Awards and memberships ==
Holland has been awarded multiple awards for his contributions to chemistry, including a [[Blavatnik Awards for Young Scientists|Blavatnik Award for Young Scientists]] in 2013,<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Patrick Holland {{!}} Blavatnik Awards for Young Scientists|url=http://blavatnikawards.org/honorees/profile/patrick-holland/|access-date=2021-06-01|website=blavatnikawards.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Department of Chemistry : University of Rochester|url=http://www.sas.rochester.edu/chm/news-events/news/2013-06-21-halland-award.html|access-date=2021-06-01|website=www.sas.rochester.edu}}</ref> a Friedrich Wilhelm Bessel Research Award of the [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation|Humboldt Foundation]] in 2016, a Fulbright Scholar Award in 2012, a [[Sloan Research Fellowship]] in 2003, and an [[National Science Foundation CAREER Awards|NSF CAREER Award]] in 2002.<ref name=":1" /> He was elected a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] in 2015.

He has served on the Editorial Boards of ''[[Chemical Science (journal)|Chemical Science]]'' and ''[[Chemical Society Reviews]]'' since 2019, and was previously on the Editorial Boards of ''[[Inorganic Chemistry (journal)|Inorganic Chemistry]]'' (2012-2014) and the ''[[Journal of Biological Inorganic Chemistry]]'' (2009-2012).

== Personal life ==
Holland is a piano soloist and accompanist for choirs, vocalists, instrumentalists, and musicals in his spare time. He has also sung with choruses such as the [[San Francisco Symphony Chorus]], and currently sings with the Yale Camerata.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Chemistry Seminar: Dr. Patrick Holland, Yale University|url=https://calendar.hope.edu/event/chemistry_seminar_1372|access-date=2021-06-01|website=Hope College Calendar|language=en}}</ref>

Holland is married to [https://www.newhaven.edu/faculty-staff-profiles/maggie-holland.php Maggie Langford Holland], another Princeton graduate.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Patrick Holland's Personal Biography {{!}} The Holland Group|url=https://holland.chem.yale.edu/people/patrick-holland/personalbio|access-date=2021-06-01|website=holland.chem.yale.edu}}</ref>
